note: Literature: unseen poems/prose with appreciation questions + devices inside quoted lines; CRS and IRS: situation-based application of the set narratives.

passages.title: Harmattan (unseen poem)
passages.text:
The harmattan creeps in on dusty feet,
it wraps the town in a grey and silent shawl;
the mango leaves hang tired in the heat,
and cracked lips wait for rain that will not fall.

Yet in the compound Grandma hums her song,
her voice a thread that stitches dawn to dusk;
she says the dry wind cannot stay for long,
that every seed lies waiting in its husk.

So I will keep my hope the way she keeps
her rosary of years, bead after bead,
until the first fat drop of April leaps
and wakes the patient sleeper in the seed.

passages.title: Hawker (unseen poem)
passages.text:
'Buy your groundnut! Buy your groundnut!'
Amaka's voice climbs over the horns of Upper Iweka,
a small bird against a storm of engines.
Her tray is a crown she never asked to wear;
beneath it, the school books her mother sold
still turn their pages in her head.
'Buy your groundnut! Buy your groundnut!'
The sun beats its drum upon her back,
the children of tomorrow pass her by in yellow buses,
and nobody asks her name.
What is the price of a childhood?
Ask the traffic. Ask the tray. Ask the silence at home.

passages.title: Unseen prose extract
passages.text: I did not cry when they read my father's will. I had done my crying years before, on the night he came home from the mill with his right hand wrapped in a bloody cloth and told us, quite calmly, that we would manage. We managed. My mother sold akara at the junction; I hawked her wares before school and after it, and my father, with his one good hand, taught me to read from newspapers that other people had thrown away. So when the lawyer announced that everything - the house, the small plot in the village, the savings nobody knew he had - was to go to my stepbrother Emeka, who had not visited in eleven years, I merely nodded. Emeka wept loudly. I remember thinking that he had not learnt, as I had, that some things are worth more than a house. Then I went outside and sat on the step where my father used to sit, and I waited to feel something.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The mood created in the first stanza of the poem is one of
questions.explanation: Dusty, grey, silent, tired leaves and cracked lips all build a tired, gloomy atmosphere.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'The harmattan creeps in on dusty feet' is an example of
questions.explanation: The wind is given a human action (creeping in on feet) — personification.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In 'her voice a thread that stitches dawn to dusk', the poet uses
questions.explanation: The voice is directly identified with a thread, without 'like' or 'as' — a metaphor.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The rhyme scheme of the first stanza is
questions.explanation: feet/heat rhyme (a) and shawl/fall rhyme (b), alternating: abab.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'The patient sleeper in the seed' most likely stands for
questions.A: Grandma's tiredness after a long day's work
questions.B: the dust that the harmattan leaves behind
questions.C: new life and hope waiting for the rain
questions.D: the poet's fear that April will never come
questions.explanation: The seed 'waiting in its husk' will be woken by the first rain; it symbolises the hope the speaker keeps alive through the dry season.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The repeated line 'Buy your groundnut! Buy your groundnut!' is an example of
questions.explanation: A line repeated at intervals in a poem is a refrain; here it also imitates the hawker's cry.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'a small bird against a storm of engines' suggests that Amaka's voice is
questions.A: loud and commanding above the traffic
questions.B: angry and defiant towards the drivers
questions.D: frail and easily drowned by the traffic
questions.explanation: A small bird against a storm is weak and overpowered — her voice is lost in the noise of the vehicles.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The device used in 'Her tray is a crown she never asked to wear' is
questions.explanation: The tray is directly called a crown (a burden imposed like royalty's duty) — a metaphor.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'What is the price of a childhood?' is
questions.explanation: The question is asked for effect; no answer is expected, and the next line replies only with more questions.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The poet's attitude towards Amaka is one of
questions.explanation: Every image (the sold books, the crown she never asked for, nobody asking her name) invites pity for a child denied school.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The passage is narrated from the
questions.explanation: The narrator speaks as 'I' and takes part in the events.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The narrator's account of the night the father came home injured is an example of
questions.explanation: The story moves back from the reading of the will to an earlier event — a flashback.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The contrast between Emeka's loud weeping and the narrator's silence chiefly serves to
questions.A: show that Emeka loved his father more than the narrator did
questions.B: suggest that the lawyer had forged the father's will
questions.C: prove that the narrator is heartless and unfeeling
questions.D: highlight the irony that the absent son displays the most grief
questions.explanation: Emeka, who stayed away for eleven years, weeps loudly while the child who suffered alongside the father stays quiet — an ironic reversal of what we expect.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: 'some things are worth more than a house' refers to
questions.A: the savings that nobody knew the father had
questions.B: the small plot of land in the village
questions.C: the love, values and learning the father gave the narrator
questions.D: the akara business the mother ran at the junction
questions.explanation: The narrator received the father's teaching and example, which he/she values above the property Emeka inherits.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The narrator can best be described as
questions.explanation: He/she 'merely nodded', reflects calmly and shows no resentment — self-controlled maturity, even while numb with grief.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: In 'The wind whispered secrets to the sleeping village', the poet uses
questions.explanation: The wind is given the human ability to whisper secrets.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'He fought like a wounded lion' is an example of
questions.explanation: The comparison is made with 'like' — a simile.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Sadly, Sunday's sermon sent Sam to sleep' illustrates
questions.explanation: The repetition of the initial 's' consonant sound is alliteration.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'I have told you a million times to shut that door' is an example of
questions.explanation: Deliberate exaggeration for effect is hyperbole.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The deafening silence of the empty hall' contains
questions.explanation: Two contradictory words placed together (deafening silence) form an oxymoron.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: In 'The crown announced new taxes', the word 'crown' is an example of
questions.explanation: Something closely associated with a thing (the crown) is used to stand for it (the monarchy/government) — metonymy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: In 'We need more hands on the farm', 'hands' is an example of
questions.explanation: A part (hands) stands for the whole (workers) — synecdoche.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The bees buzzed and the kettle hissed on the fire' illustrates
questions.explanation: 'Buzzed' and 'hissed' imitate the sounds they describe.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: A fire station burns to the ground while the firemen are attending a safety lecture. This is an example of
questions.explanation: The outcome is the opposite of what one would expect — situational irony.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: On stage a king says, 'I trust my brother with my life', although the audience has just watched the brother plot his murder. This is
questions.explanation: The audience knows something the character does not — dramatic irony.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Our dear teacher has gone to rest with his ancestors' is an example of
questions.explanation: A mild expression replaces a harsh one (he has died) — euphemism.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'O Death, where is thy sting?' illustrates
questions.explanation: Addressing an absent person or an abstraction (Death) as if present is apostrophe.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The child is father of the man' is an example of
questions.explanation: The statement seems self-contradictory yet contains a truth (childhood shapes the adult) — a paradox.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'Man proposes, God disposes' illustrates
questions.explanation: Contrasting ideas are set against each other in a balanced structure — antithesis.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'She is not unkind to strangers' is an example of
questions.explanation: Understatement by denying the opposite (not unkind = kind) is litotes.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The champion met his Waterloo in the final match' contains
questions.explanation: A reference to Napoleon's defeat at Waterloo — a historical allusion meaning a final defeat.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'In one week he lost his wife, his fortune and his favourite pen' is an example of
questions.explanation: The series descends suddenly from the serious to the trivial — anticlimax (bathos).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The bank's employees lost interest in their jobs' relies on
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is used in two senses at once (enthusiasm; money earned on deposits) — a pun.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Literary Devices and Figures of Speech
questions.q: 'The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain' illustrates
questions.explanation: The same vowel sound (/eɪ/) is repeated in rain, Spain, mainly, plain — assonance.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character alone on stage speaks his private thoughts aloud so that the audience can hear them. This is
questions.explanation: A soliloquy is a speech made by a character alone on stage revealing his thoughts.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: During a conversation, a character turns and makes a brief remark heard by the audience but supposedly not by the other characters. This is
questions.explanation: An aside is a short remark to the audience that other characters are assumed not to hear.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A play presents a noble hero whose downfall and death are brought about by a weakness in his own character. The play is a
questions.explanation: A serious play ending in the ruin of the protagonist through his tragic flaw (hamartia) is a tragedy.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem has fourteen lines, three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming abab cdcd efef gg. It is
questions.explanation: Three quatrains and a closing couplet with that rhyme scheme is the English (Shakespearean) sonnet; the Petrarchan sonnet has an octave and a sestet.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A poem written to mourn the death of a person is
questions.explanation: An elegy is a poem of mourning or lament for the dead.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A long narrative poem recounting the heroic deeds of a legendary figure is
questions.explanation: Epics such as the Iliad or Sundiata are long narrative poems about heroes.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Lines of unrhymed iambic pentameter, such as most of Shakespeare's plays, are written in
questions.explanation: Blank verse is unrhymed iambic pentameter; free verse has no regular metre at all.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel that tells its story entirely through letters exchanged between the characters is
questions.explanation: Epistolary comes from 'epistle' (letter).

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A novel that traces the moral and psychological growth of its main character from childhood to adulthood is called
questions.explanation: Bildungsroman is the novel of formation or growing up.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Animal Farm uses talking animals to ridicule the abuses of power after a revolution. The work is best described as
questions.explanation: It is a fable (animals as characters teaching a lesson) used as political satire.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a tragedy, a scene of humour introduced to ease the tension is called
questions.explanation: Comic relief lightens the mood temporarily, e.g. the porter scene in Macbeth.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The point in a play or novel where the conflict reaches its highest intensity is the
questions.explanation: The climax is the turning point of greatest tension.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The part of the plot in which the loose ends are tied up after the climax is the
questions.explanation: Denouement (resolution) follows the climax and settles the outcome.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: Early in a novel, a character remarks that the old bridge 'will kill someone one day'; in the final chapter the hero drowns when it collapses. The early remark is an example of
questions.explanation: A hint of what is to come later in the story is foreshadowing.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A story in which characters and events stand for abstract ideas such as greed, justice or salvation is
questions.explanation: In allegory the surface story carries a second, symbolic meaning throughout.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A narrator who reports the thoughts and feelings of every character and comments on events is
questions.explanation: The omniscient ('all-knowing') narrator has access to all characters' minds.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.topic: Narrative Techniques and Point of View
questions.q: A short story is told by a ten-year-old who does not understand the adult events he describes, so the reader knows more than he does. The narrator is
questions.explanation: A narrator whose account cannot be fully trusted because of ignorance, youth or bias is an unreliable narrator.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: A character who is arrogant at the start of a novel but, after suffering, becomes humble and generous is
questions.explanation: A character who undergoes significant change is dynamic; flat and static characters remain the same.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a play, the honest, gentle brother is placed beside the cruel, scheming one so that each shows up the other's qualities. The gentle brother is a
questions.explanation: A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with and highlight those of another.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: The main character of a story who drives the action is the
questions.explanation: The protagonist is the central character; the antagonist opposes him or her.

questions.subject: Literature in English
questions.q: In a poem the lines run on into one another without punctuation at the end of each line. This technique is called
questions.explanation: Enjambment is the running-on of sense from one line to the next; a caesura is a pause within a line.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: After his brothers sold him into slavery and he later became governor of Egypt, Joseph told them, 'You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good.' This statement teaches that
questions.C: Joseph had forgotten what they did
questions.D: God can bring good out of human wickedness
questions.explanation: Genesis 50:20 shows God's sovereignty and providence: He turned the brothers' evil plan into the saving of many lives.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The sign of the covenant God made with Abraham was
questions.explanation: In Genesis 17 every male of Abraham's household was to be circumcised as the sign of the covenant; the rainbow was the sign given to Noah.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Moses' father-in-law Jethro saw him judging the people alone from morning till evening and advised him to
questions.A: stop judging the people and leave it to the priests
questions.B: hand over all the judging to Aaron and his sons
questions.C: send the quarrelsome people back to Egypt
questions.D: appoint able men to judge minor cases while he handled the difficult ones
questions.explanation: Exodus 18: Jethro taught delegation — choose capable, God-fearing men as rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A class captain who divides duties among group leaders instead of doing everything himself is applying the lesson Moses learnt from
questions.explanation: Jethro's counsel to Moses (Exodus 18) is the biblical model of delegation of responsibility.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: During the wilderness journey God guided the Israelites by day and by night with
questions.A: a pillar of cloud and a pillar of fire
questions.explanation: Exodus 13:21 — a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night led the way.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Eli the priest was judged by God mainly because he
questions.A: offered sacrifices that were not according to the law
questions.B: refused to train the boy Samuel in the service of God
questions.C: failed to restrain his sons Hophni and Phinehas from their wickedness
questions.D: stole the offerings of the people from the sanctuary
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 2–3: Eli honoured his sons above God by not restraining them, so judgment came on his house.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Samuel told Saul, 'To obey is better than sacrifice', after Saul
questions.A: built an altar to the Lord without Samuel's permission
questions.B: consulted the medium at Endor about the Philistines
questions.C: refused to lead Israel against the Philistines
questions.D: spared King Agag and the best of the Amalekite animals contrary to God's command
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 15: Saul kept the best animals 'to sacrifice' instead of destroying everything as commanded, and lost the kingdom.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: Nathan told David a parable about a rich man who took a poor man's only ewe lamb. The purpose of the parable was to
questions.A: praise David for his generosity to the poor
questions.B: ask David to provide a lamb for the sacrifice
questions.C: make David condemn himself for taking Uriah's wife
questions.D: warn David about the rebellion of Absalom
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12: when David condemned the rich man, Nathan said, 'You are the man', exposing his sin with Bathsheba.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: A Man after God's Own Heart
questions.q: When Nathan confronted David over his sin with Bathsheba, David's response was to
questions.A: order that Nathan be put to death
questions.B: deny the charge and demand witnesses
questions.C: confess, saying 'I have sinned against the Lord'
questions.explanation: 2 Samuel 12:13 — David's immediate confession and repentance (see also Psalm 51) is why he is called a man after God's own heart.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders and followed the advice of his young friends to increase the people's burdens. The result was that
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12: ten tribes revolted under Jeroboam, leaving Rehoboam with Judah and Benjamin.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When God asked Solomon at Gibeon what he wanted, Solomon asked for
questions.A: a long life on the throne of Israel
questions.C: the death of all his enemies
questions.D: an understanding mind to govern the people
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3: Solomon asked for wisdom to discern between good and evil, and God added riches and honour.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ahab wanted Naboth's vineyard. Jezebel arranged for Naboth to be falsely accused and stoned. The prophet who condemned Ahab for this was
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21: Elijah met Ahab in the vineyard and pronounced judgment on his house.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Gehazi, Elisha's servant, secretly collected gifts from Naaman after his master had refused them. His punishment was
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:27 — Naaman's leprosy clung to Gehazi and his descendants.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A cashier who quietly pockets money a customer left behind, thinking no one saw her, is repeating the sin of
questions.explanation: Like Gehazi (2 Kings 5), she takes for herself what she has no right to, believing it hidden.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: On Mount Carmel, Elijah proved that the Lord is God when
questions.A: rain fell after three and a half years of drought
questions.B: Ahab repented and destroyed the altars of Baal
questions.C: the prophets of Baal fled to the brook Kishon
questions.D: fire from heaven consumed his water-soaked sacrifice
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18: the fire fell on Elijah's drenched altar and the people cried, 'The Lord, he is God.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The reforms of King Josiah began when
questions.A: he defeated the Assyrians at Megiddo
questions.B: the prophet Isaiah rebuked him for idolatry
questions.C: the Book of the Law was found in the temple during repairs
questions.D: he saw a vision of the Lord in the temple
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 22: Hilkiah found the Book of the Law; Josiah tore his clothes, renewed the covenant and destroyed idolatry.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Nehemiah, cup-bearer to the Persian king, wept and prayed when he heard that
questions.A: the temple had been burnt by the Babylonians
questions.B: the Jews in Jerusalem were worshipping Baal
questions.C: Ezra the scribe had died in Jerusalem
questions.D: the walls of Jerusalem were broken down and its gates burnt
questions.explanation: Nehemiah 1: the report about Jerusalem's broken walls led him to seek permission to rebuild them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were thrown into the fiery furnace because they
questions.A: refused to bow down to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image
questions.explanation: Daniel 3: they told the king that even if God did not deliver them, they would not serve his gods.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Daniel was thrown into the lions' den because he
questions.A: refused to eat the king's meat
questions.C: continued to pray to God despite the king's decree
questions.D: refused to interpret the writing on the wall
questions.explanation: Daniel 6: jealous officials tricked Darius into a decree, and Daniel kept praying openly three times a day.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jonah was angry after preaching in Nineveh because
questions.A: the people of Nineveh stoned him
questions.B: the great fish swallowed him a second time
questions.C: the king of Nineveh refused to listen to him
questions.D: God spared the city when the people repented
questions.explanation: Jonah 4: he resented God's mercy on Israel's enemy; God used the plant and worm to teach him compassion.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: Amos condemned the people of Israel who 'sell the righteous for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals'. Amos was speaking against
questions.A: the worship of golden calves at Bethel
questions.B: the profaning of the Sabbath and new moon
questions.C: social injustice and oppression of the poor
questions.explanation: Amos 2:6 and 5:24 ('let justice roll down like waters') attack corruption and exploitation of the poor.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Social Justice, True Religion and Divine Love
questions.q: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, an unfaithful woman, in order to
questions.A: punish Hosea for his earlier disobedience
questions.B: qualify Hosea to serve as a priest
questions.C: show that marriage to a foreigner is sinful
questions.D: illustrate God's steadfast love for unfaithful Israel
questions.explanation: Hosea 1–3: Hosea's love for his adulterous wife pictured God's continued love for idolatrous Israel.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In his vision in the temple, Isaiah cried 'Woe is me! For I am a man of unclean lips.' His lips were then cleansed by
questions.A: water from the laver in the temple
questions.B: the blood of a lamb sprinkled by a priest
questions.C: a burning coal carried by a seraph
questions.D: the anointing oil of the high priest
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6: a seraph touched his mouth with a live coal and declared his guilt taken away; then he said, 'Here am I! Send me.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ezekiel's vision of the valley of dry bones that came to life symbolised
questions.A: the resurrection of Jesus on the third day
questions.B: the creation of man from the dust of the ground
questions.C: the destruction of Babylon by the Persians
questions.D: the restoration of the exiled nation of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 37:11 — 'These bones are the whole house of Israel'; God would bring them back to their land.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.q: In the wilderness the devil said to Jesus, 'If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread.' Jesus replied that
questions.A: man shall not live by bread alone
questions.B: you shall not tempt the Lord your God
questions.C: you shall worship the Lord only
questions.explanation: Matthew 4:4 quotes Deuteronomy 8:3; the other replies belong to the second and third temptations.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A man told Jesus, 'I will follow you wherever you go.' Jesus answered, 'Foxes have holes and birds have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.' Jesus meant that
questions.A: the man should first buy a house for them
questions.B: he was homeless and needed the man's help
questions.C: discipleship demands readiness to bear hardship
questions.D: the man should go home to his family
questions.explanation: Luke 9:57–62 sets out the cost of discipleship: sacrifice, urgency and no looking back.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Four men could not reach Jesus because of the crowd, so they lowered their paralysed friend through the roof. Jesus first said to the paralytic,
questions.explanation: Mark 2:5 — Jesus forgave his sins first, and healed him to prove that the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus healed ten lepers, but only one returned to give thanks. That man was
questions.explanation: Luke 17:16 — the grateful one was a Samaritan, a 'foreigner', which highlights ingratitude among Jesus' own people.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, the priest and the Levite passed by the wounded man. Jesus told this parable in answer to the question
questions.C: 'What must I do to be saved?'
questions.explanation: Luke 10:29 — a lawyer asked, 'And who is my neighbour?'; Jesus ended, 'Go and do likewise.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A student helps an injured stranger from a rival school get to the hospital, paying for his treatment. He is putting into practice the parable of the
questions.explanation: Practical mercy to someone outside one's own group is the lesson of the good Samaritan (Luke 10).

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: In the parable of the unforgiving servant, the servant whose debt of ten thousand talents was cancelled then
questions.A: forgave his fellow servant who owed him a hundred denarii
questions.B: thanked the king and served him faithfully thereafter
questions.C: paid off his fellow servant's debt to the king
questions.D: seized a fellow servant who owed him a small sum and had him jailed
questions.explanation: Matthew 18:21–35 answers Peter's question about forgiving 'seventy times seven'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A rich man planned to pull down his barns and build bigger ones, saying to himself, 'Eat, drink, be merry.' God called him a fool because
questions.A: he laid up treasure for himself but was not rich towards God
questions.B: he refused to share his harvest with his labourers
questions.C: he had cheated his neighbours to acquire the land
questions.D: he did not pay tithes on the harvest to the priests
questions.explanation: Luke 12:16–21 warns against covetousness: 'one's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A boy is slapped by a classmate and, instead of retaliating, walks away and later helps the same boy with his homework. He is obeying Jesus' teaching to
questions.A: demand an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
questions.B: judge not, that you be not judged
questions.C: turn the other cheek and love your enemies
questions.D: seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:38–48 replaces retaliation with non-resistance and love for enemies.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus asked, 'Why do you see the speck in your brother's eye but do not notice the log in your own eye?' He was warning against
questions.explanation: Matthew 7:1–5 — 'Judge not, that you be not judged.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked, 'Who do you say that I am?' The disciple who answered 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' was
questions.explanation: Matthew 16:16 — Jesus replied that flesh and blood had not revealed this to Peter but the Father in heaven.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the transfiguration the two Old Testament figures who appeared talking with Jesus were
questions.explanation: Matthew 17:3 — Moses (the Law) and Elijah (the Prophets) appeared, and Peter offered to build three booths.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.q: When Jesus drove out the traders from the temple he said, 'My house shall be called a house of prayer, but you have made it
questions.explanation: Matthew 21:13 combines Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: At the Last Supper, Jesus washed the disciples' feet in order to
questions.A: fulfil the requirements of the Passover law
questions.B: show the disciples that Judas was clean
questions.C: prepare them for baptism with the Holy Spirit
questions.D: teach them humble service to one another
questions.explanation: John 13:14–15 — 'I have given you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Trials and the Death of Jesus
questions.q: Pilate offered to release one prisoner at the feast. The crowd chose
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:15–26 — the crowd, stirred by the chief priests, demanded Barabbas and shouted 'Crucify him' about Jesus.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Two disciples walking to Emmaus recognised the risen Jesus only when he
questions.explanation: Luke 24:30–31 — their eyes were opened at the breaking of bread.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Thomas said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks. When he later saw Jesus he exclaimed,
questions.D: 'Truly this was the Son of God'
questions.explanation: John 20:28; Jesus replied, 'Blessed are those who have not seen and yet believe.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Jesus said, 'I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.' By this he contrasted himself with
questions.A: the Pharisees who were faithful shepherds
questions.D: the hireling who flees when the wolf comes
questions.explanation: John 10:11–13 — the hired hand cares nothing for the sheep and abandons them.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Ananias and Sapphira died because they
questions.A: lied to the Holy Spirit about the price of the land they sold
questions.B: refused to sell their land for the common fund
questions.C: stole money from the apostles' common purse
questions.explanation: Acts 5:1–11 — the sin was not keeping part of the money but pretending to give all of it.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Holy Spirit and the Mission of the Church
questions.q: On the day of Pentecost the disciples spoke in other tongues, and the crowd from many nations
questions.A: could not understand a word they said
questions.C: each heard them speaking in his own language
questions.D: asked them for money and food
questions.explanation: Acts 2:6–8; Peter then preached and about three thousand were baptised.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Sanhedrin ordered Peter and John to stop preaching in the name of Jesus, they replied that
questions.D: they must obey God rather than men
questions.explanation: Acts 4:19–20 and 5:29 — 'We cannot but speak of what we have seen and heard.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Gamaliel advised the Sanhedrin to leave the apostles alone because
questions.A: a work of God cannot be overthrown by men
questions.B: they were Roman citizens protected by law
questions.C: Peter had healed his son of a fever
questions.D: the crowd would riot if they were harmed
questions.explanation: Acts 5:34–39 — he cited the failed movements of Theudas and Judas the Galilean.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Peter's vision of a sheet full of unclean animals, before he visited Cornelius, taught him that
questions.A: Jews were now free to eat pork and other unclean foods
questions.B: the law of Moses had been abolished completely
questions.C: God shows no partiality and Gentiles may receive the gospel
questions.D: Cornelius should first become a Jew by circumcision
questions.explanation: Acts 10:28, 34 — 'God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean.'

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: The Council of Jerusalem decided that Gentile converts
questions.A: must be circumcised according to the custom of Moses
questions.B: could not be baptised until they kept the Sabbath
questions.C: must keep the whole law of Moses to be saved
questions.D: need not be circumcised, but must avoid idol food, blood and immorality
questions.explanation: Acts 15:19–20 records James' judgment, sent by letter to Antioch.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul cited Abraham, who 'believed God, and it was counted to him as righteousness', to prove that a person is justified by
questions.explanation: Romans 4:1–5 and Galatians 3:6 — Abraham was counted righteous before he was circumcised or the law was given.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul called the law 'our custodian (schoolmaster) until Christ came' to show that the law
questions.A: saves all those who keep it perfectly
questions.B: is no longer to be read in the churches
questions.C: was meant to lead people to Christ, who justifies by faith
questions.D: was given only to the Gentiles, not the Jews
questions.explanation: Galatians 3:24–25 — once faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote, 'If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; the old has passed away.' A convert who gives up cheating in examinations and lying is demonstrating
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Colossians 3:5–10 describe putting off the old nature and its practices.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.q: According to Paul, believers are 'heirs of God and fellow heirs with Christ' provided that they
questions.A: suffer with him so that they may be glorified with him
questions.B: pay their tithes faithfully to the church
questions.C: are circumcised according to the law
questions.D: speak in tongues as evidence of the Spirit
questions.explanation: Romans 8:16–17: the Spirit bears witness that we are children of God, and therefore heirs, 'provided we suffer with him'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul urged the Philippians to have the mind of Christ, who 'though he was in the form of God ... emptied himself, taking the form of a servant'. The virtue being taught is
questions.explanation: Philippians 2:5–11 — Christ's self-emptying is the model of humility; therefore God highly exalted him.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul wrote to Philemon asking him to receive back Onesimus, his runaway slave,
questions.A: as a runaway slave to be punished severely
questions.B: as Paul's replacement in the Colossian church
questions.C: only after Onesimus had repaid what he stole
questions.D: no longer as a slave but as a beloved brother
questions.explanation: Philemon 15–17 — Paul offered to pay whatever Onesimus owed.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul compared the church to a human body with many members to teach that
questions.A: every member's gift is needed and none should despise another's
questions.B: some spiritual gifts are useless to the church
questions.C: only the apostles and prophets really matter
questions.D: the body can manage without its weaker parts
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:12–27 — 'the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of you'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul praised the Macedonian churches because, in deep poverty, they
questions.C: gave generously, even beyond their means
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 8:1–5; and 9:7 — 'God loves a cheerful giver'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: A Christian who pays his taxes honestly and obeys traffic laws, even when nobody is watching, is following Paul's teaching in Romans 13 that
questions.A: Christians are above the laws of the state
questions.B: governing authorities are instituted by God and must be obeyed
questions.C: taxes are unjust and need not be paid
questions.D: only the laws of the church are binding
questions.explanation: Romans 13:1–7 — 'pay taxes to whom taxes are due, respect to whom respect is due'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Thessalonians, 'If anyone will not work, let him not eat', because some members were
questions.A: too poor to find any work in the city of Thessalonica
questions.B: idle busybodies living off other members
questions.C: working on the Sabbath against the law
questions.D: refusing to pay tithes to the elders
questions.explanation: 2 Thessalonians 3:6–12 — Paul himself worked night and day so as not to burden anyone.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Thessalonians that the day of the Lord will come 'like a thief in the night'. He meant that Christians should
questions.A: calculate the exact date from the prophets
questions.B: stop working and wait on the mountains
questions.C: be watchful and live soberly since the time is unknown
questions.D: sell their property and give to the church
questions.explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:1–11 — 'let us keep awake and be sober'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James condemned church members who gave a rich man in fine clothes the best seat while telling a poor man to sit on the floor. This sin is
questions.explanation: James 2:1–9 — 'if you show partiality, you commit sin'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: James gave Elijah as an example of effective prayer because Elijah
questions.A: was an angel sent from heaven
questions.B: prayed for drought and later for rain, and both happened
questions.C: prayed in the temple three times every day
questions.explanation: James 5:16–18 — 'The prayer of a righteous man has great power'; Elijah was 'a man of like nature with ourselves'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Simon the sorcerer offered the apostles money so that he too could give the Holy Spirit by laying on hands. Peter's response teaches that
questions.A: spiritual gifts can be bought by the rich
questions.B: the gift of God cannot be obtained with money
questions.D: money should be given to apostles
questions.explanation: Acts 8:18–24 — 'Your silver perish with you'; buying church office is still called simony.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Joseph refused the advances of Potiphar's wife, saying, 'How can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?' He was later
questions.explanation: Genesis 39 — Joseph chose purity at great cost, yet God was with him in prison.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: Paul told the Corinthians to 'flee from sexual immorality' because the believer's body is
questions.A: his own to use as he likes
questions.B: a temple of the Holy Spirit, bought with a price
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 6:18–20 — 'glorify God in your body'.

questions.subject: Christian Religious Studies
questions.q: According to Paul in 1 Corinthians 13, a person who speaks in tongues, has prophetic powers and gives away all he has, but has not love,
questions.A: is the greatest in the kingdom
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 13:1–3; 'the greatest of these is love'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first verses of the Qur'an revealed to Prophet Muhammad (SAW) in the cave of Hira began with the command
questions.explanation: Surah Al-'Alaq (96:1–5) opens 'Read in the name of your Lord who created', brought by the angel Jibril.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah of Salah. It is also known as
questions.A: Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book)
questions.B: Ayat al-Kursi (the Verse of the Throne)
questions.D: Khatm al-Qur'an (the Seal of the Qur'an)
questions.explanation: Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab and As-Sab' al-Mathani (the seven oft-repeated verses).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Surah that declares 'Say: He is Allah, the One; Allah the Eternal; He begets not, nor was He begotten' is
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) is the clearest statement of Tawhid and is said to equal a third of the Qur'an in reward.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Surah Al-Asr teaches that all mankind is in loss except those who
questions.A: are wealthy, powerful and respected in society
questions.B: believe, do righteous deeds, and enjoin one another to truth and patience
questions.C: fast every Monday and Thursday throughout the year
questions.D: perform Hajj and Umrah every year of their lives
questions.explanation: Surah 103 gives four conditions for salvation: faith, good deeds, mutual counsel to truth and to patience.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A student fasts only so that his classmates will praise his piety. According to the Hadith 'Actions are judged by intentions', his fast
questions.A: is doubly rewarded because others were encouraged
questions.B: earns no reward with Allah because the intention was to be seen
questions.C: is fully rewarded because he abstained from food and drink
questions.D: counts as a voluntary fast of the highest grade
questions.explanation: The first Hadith in Bukhari: 'every person will get what he intended' — worship done for show (riya') is worthless.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A trader hides the fault in the goods he sells. The Prophet (SAW) said of such a person:
questions.B: 'Whoever cheats is not one of us'
questions.explanation: The Prophet found wet grain hidden under dry grain in the market and declared, 'Man ghashshana fa laysa minna'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'The strong man is not the one who overcomes others in wrestling, but the one who ______.'
questions.explanation: The Hadith (Bukhari and Muslim) redefines strength as self-control.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: According to the Hadith, 'None of you truly believes until he
questions.A: loves for his brother what he loves for himself'
questions.B: performs Hajj to the House of Allah'
questions.C: memorises the whole of the Qur'an'
questions.D: gives away all his wealth in charity'
questions.explanation: Reported by Bukhari and Muslim; it is the basis of Islamic brotherhood.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Tawhid and the Oneness of Allah
questions.q: A man wears a charm because he believes it, and not Allah, protects him from harm. This belief is
questions.explanation: Attributing power that belongs to Allah alone to anything else is shirk, the gravest sin (Qur'an 4:48).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Ayat al-Kursi states that 'neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him'. This describes Allah's attribute of being
questions.B: Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim (the Most Gracious, Most Merciful)
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:255 begins 'Allah — there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who loses his business in a fire says, 'This is from Allah; I accept it and will work again.' He is showing belief in
questions.explanation: Acceptance of what Allah has decreed, good or bad, is belief in Qadar, the sixth article of faith.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The angel responsible for bringing revelation to the prophets is
questions.explanation: Jibril (Gabriel) brought the Qur'an to Prophet Muhammad; Mika'il oversees rain and provision; Israfil blows the trumpet.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The total number of obligatory (fard) rak'ahs a Muslim prays in the five daily prayers is
questions.explanation: Fajr 2 + Zuhr 4 + Asr 4 + Maghrib 3 + Isha 4 = 17 rak'ahs.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A traveller on a journey of about 300 km shortens Zuhr from four rak'ahs to two. This concession is called
questions.explanation: Qasr is the shortening of four-rak'ah prayers on a journey (Qur'an 4:101); Jam' is combining two prayers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim in the desert finds no water for ablution before prayer. He should
questions.D: wait until he reaches a town
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:6 permits tayammum (dry ablution) when water is unavailable or its use is harmful.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Alhaji Musa has kept ₦4,000,000 in savings, above the nisab, for a full lunar year. The Zakat due on it is

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT among the eight categories entitled to receive Zakat according to Qur'an 9:60?
questions.B: those in debt who cannot repay
questions.D: the wealthy relatives of the giver
questions.explanation: The eight recipients are the poor, the needy, Zakat collectors, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, captives, debtors, in the cause of Allah, and wayfarers.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Zakat paid by every Muslim who can afford it before the Eid-ul-Fitr prayer, on behalf of each member of the household, is
questions.explanation: Zakat al-Fitr purifies the fasting person and feeds the poor on the day of Eid.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A pregnant woman fears that fasting will harm her baby. Islamic law allows her to
questions.B: break the fast and make up the missed days later
questions.C: abandon fasting permanently with no compensation
questions.explanation: The sick, travellers, pregnant and nursing women may postpone the fast and make it up (Qur'an 2:184–185).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A very old man is permanently unable to fast in Ramadan. He should
questions.A: make up the days after Ramadan when he feels stronger
questions.B: pay fidyah by feeding a poor person for each day missed
questions.C: perform Hajj instead of fasting that year
questions.D: pray extra rak'ahs each night in place of the fast
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:184 — those who cannot fast at all give fidyah (feeding a needy person per day).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: While fasting, a man forgetfully eats a piece of bread. His fast
questions.A: is broken and must be repeated
questions.B: remains valid; he should continue fasting
questions.C: is broken and requires 60 days' expiation
questions.D: is converted to a voluntary fast
questions.explanation: The Prophet said whoever eats or drinks forgetfully should complete his fast, for it was Allah who fed him.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The rite of Hajj without which the pilgrimage is invalid, performed on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, is
questions.explanation: The Prophet said 'Al-Hajj Arafah' — Hajj is Arafah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Hajj is obligatory on a Muslim
questions.A: every year for as long as he lives
questions.B: once in a lifetime, if physically and financially able
questions.C: only after he reaches the age of sixty
questions.D: only if he is a man and head of a family
questions.explanation: Qur'an 3:97 — pilgrimage is a duty owed to Allah by those who can find a way to it.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The walking seven times between the hills of Safa and Marwah during Hajj commemorates
questions.A: the Prophet's Hijrah from Makkah to Madinah
questions.B: Hajar's search for water for her son Isma'il
questions.C: the Muslims' march to the battle of Badr
questions.D: the digging of the trench around Madinah
questions.explanation: Sa'y re-enacts Hajar running between the two hills before the well of Zamzam gushed forth.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) described the struggle against one's own evil desires as
questions.C: hijrah (migration for the sake of Allah)
questions.explanation: Self-discipline against the lower self is called the greater jihad; armed struggle in defence of the faith is the lesser.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Prophet Muhammad (SAW) was born in Makkah in the year
questions.explanation: He was born in 'Am al-Fil, the year Abrahah's army with an elephant attacked the Ka'bah and was destroyed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: When the Quraysh clans quarrelled over who should replace the Black Stone during the rebuilding of the Ka'bah, Muhammad (SAW) settled it by
questions.A: choosing his own clan, Banu Hashim, to place it
questions.B: placing the stone on a cloth so that all the clan leaders lifted it together
questions.C: asking his uncle Abu Talib to decide between the clans
questions.D: leaving the stone on the ground until the quarrel ended
questions.explanation: The incident earned him the title Al-Amin (the trustworthy) and shows his wisdom and justice even before prophethood.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Islamic calendar begins from the year of
questions.A: the Prophet's birth in the year of the Elephant
questions.B: the first revelation in the cave of Hira
questions.C: the Prophet's migration from Makkah to Madinah (622 CE)
questions.D: the conquest of Makkah by the Muslims
questions.explanation: Caliph Umar fixed the Hijrah of 622 CE as year 1 AH.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: During the Hijrah, the Prophet (SAW) and Abu Bakr hid for three days in
questions.explanation: A spider's web and a dove's nest at the mouth of the cave of Thawr turned the pursuers away.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Leader
questions.q: On entering Madinah, the Prophet (SAW) established a written agreement between the Muslims, the Jews and other tribes of the city, known as
questions.explanation: The Sahifah guaranteed mutual defence and religious freedom, creating one community (ummah) under the Prophet's authority.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: The Prophet Muhammad as a Model
questions.q: On the conquest of Makkah, the Prophet (SAW) said to the Makkans who had persecuted him for years, 'Go, you are free.' This shows his quality of
questions.explanation: He forgave his enemies at the moment of total victory, following the example of Prophet Yusuf.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: After many huffaz (memorisers of the Qur'an) died at the battle of Yamamah, the first collection of the Qur'an into a single volume was ordered by
questions.explanation: Abu Bakr, on Umar's advice, appointed Zayd ibn Thabit to compile the Qur'an; Uthman later standardised copies.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The caliph who introduced the Hijrah calendar, established the Bayt al-Mal (public treasury) departments and appointed judges in the provinces was
questions.explanation: Umar's ten-year caliphate (634–644 CE) built the administrative institutions of the Islamic state.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: On arrival in Madinah, the Prophet (SAW) paired each emigrant from Makkah (Muhajir) with a resident of Madinah (Ansar) as brothers. This bond is called
questions.explanation: The Ansar shared their homes and property with the Muhajirun, uniting the community.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following makes an Islamic marriage contract (nikah) valid?
questions.A: a lavish ceremony attended by both families
questions.B: offer and acceptance, the bride's guardian (wali), two witnesses and mahr
questions.C: registration of the marriage at a court or registry
questions.D: the couple living together for at least one year
questions.explanation: These are the essential pillars of nikah; the mahr (dower) is the wife's right, not the family's.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The waiting period (iddah) of a widow, if she is not pregnant, is
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:234; a divorced woman waits three menstrual cycles (2:228); a pregnant woman until delivery.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.topic: Rights and Duties of Parents and Children
questions.q: The Qur'an commands: 'Say not to them (your parents) a word of contempt (uff), nor repel them, but address them in terms of honour.' A son who shouts at his aged mother is violating
questions.explanation: Kindness to parents (birr al-walidayn) is placed immediately after the worship of Allah in 17:23–24.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who spreads a rumour about his neighbour without verifying it violates the Qur'anic command in Surah Al-Hujurat to
questions.A: fast on Mondays and Thursdays as expiation
questions.B: verify news brought by a wrongdoer and avoid suspicion and backbiting
questions.C: give charity in secret so the left hand does not know
questions.D: lower the voice in the Prophet's presence
questions.explanation: Qur'an 49:6 and 49:12 forbid acting on unverified reports, suspicion, spying and backbiting.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'an commands believers to 'stand out firmly for justice, as witnesses to Allah, even if it be against yourselves, or your parents or kin'. A witness who tells the truth in court although it harms his own brother is obeying
questions.explanation: Justice in Islam is owed even against oneself and one's relatives, and also to enemies (5:8).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A shopkeeper who uses a false measure to give customers less than they pay for is condemned in the Qur'an in
questions.A: Surah Al-Mutaffifin (Those Who Deal in Fraud)
questions.explanation: Surah 83 opens 'Woe to those who give less in measure and weight'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A contractor gives a government official money so that he will be awarded a road contract he does not merit. The Prophet (SAW) said about such a transaction:
questions.A: 'It is a gift, and gifts are permitted'
questions.B: 'Allah's curse is on the one who gives a bribe and the one who takes it'
questions.C: 'It is permitted if it secures lawful business'
questions.D: 'Only the one who takes the money is guilty'
questions.explanation: Reported by Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi; bribery (rishwah) is forbidden for both parties.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A bank offers a Muslim a loan of ₦1,000,000 to be repaid as ₦1,300,000 after one year. The extra ₦300,000 is
questions.C: mahr, which is the wife's right
questions.explanation: Qur'an 2:275 — 'Allah has permitted trade and forbidden riba'; any fixed increase on a loan is riba.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Which of the following foods is permitted (halal) for a Muslim?
questions.B: an animal that died of itself (carrion)
questions.C: a goat slaughtered with the name of Allah pronounced over it
questions.D: an animal slaughtered in the name of an idol
questions.explanation: Qur'an 5:3 lists carrion, blood, pork and animals dedicated to other than Allah as forbidden.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: Before deciding to meet the Makkan army outside Madinah at Uhud, the Prophet (SAW) consulted his companions and followed the majority view. This illustrates the principle of
questions.explanation: Qur'an 42:38 describes believers as those 'whose affairs are conducted by mutual consultation'.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: In his first speech as caliph, Abu Bakr said, 'Obey me so long as I obey Allah and His Messenger; if I disobey them, you owe me no obedience.' This shows that in Islam a leader
questions.A: is above the law once he has been chosen
questions.B: must be obeyed only within the limits of Allah's law
questions.C: cannot be criticised by ordinary believers
questions.D: rules by inheritance from the previous caliph
questions.explanation: Leadership in Islam is a trust (amanah) and obedience is conditional on obedience to Allah.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Qur'anic verse 'There is no compulsion in religion' (2:256) teaches that Muslims should
questions.B: not compel anyone to accept Islam
questions.explanation: Faith must be freely accepted; the Prophet protected the religious freedom of non-Muslims under his rule.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The first major battle between the Muslims and the Makkan Quraysh, in which about 313 Muslims defeated a much larger army in 2 AH (624 CE), was the battle of
questions.explanation: Badr was a decisive victory; Uhud (3 AH) followed, then the Trench (5 AH).

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: At the battle of the Trench (Khandaq), the Muslims defended Madinah by digging a ditch on the advice of
questions.explanation: Salman the Persian suggested the Persian tactic of a defensive trench; the confederates' siege failed.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim youth is offered alcohol at a party. The Qur'an (5:90) describes intoxicants, gambling and idols as
questions.B: an abomination of Satan's handiwork, to be avoided
questions.C: lawful at all times outside the month of Ramadan
questions.D: a matter of personal choice for each believer
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:90–91 commands believers to shun them so that they may prosper.

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: The Prophet (SAW) said, 'The best of you are those who are best to their wives.' A husband who treats his wife harshly is
questions.B: acting against the Prophet's teaching and example
questions.D: exempt because he provides for her
questions.explanation: Reported by Tirmidhi; the Prophet's own gentleness at home is the model (Qur'an 4:19: 'live with them in kindness').

questions.subject: Islamic Religious Studies
questions.q: A Muslim who prays, fasts and gives charity but also cheats his business partners has neglected the part of worship called
questions.explanation: Islam covers both ibadat (rituals) and mu'amalat (transactions); the Prophet said the bankrupt is one whose prayers are cancelled by wrongs done to others.
